project.name: Peat Inn
project.boundarySource: Resolved named-place location with a conservative strict settlement study buffer
project.researchNotes: Sequential place 2 of 13: every visitor category, strict boundary, all four named trail providers, local HES/NRHE completeness, construction dates, access, transport and dogs were rechecked before continuing. The Michelin-starred restaurant is not published as an Eat because this guide prioritises coffee, cake and light daytime food. Customer parking and toilets are not general public facilities.

touristAppeal.label: Limited Visitor Interest
touristAppeal.summary: Peat Inn is a recognisable hamlet centred on a celebrated destination restaurant and crossed by St Margaret’s Way, but the restaurant is full fine dining rather than the required café/light-lunch offer and there are no independent public facilities. It remains selector-only.
touristAppeal.dogAccessSummary: The long pilgrimage route provides lawful outdoor access, with close control required around roads, farms and livestock; no dog-welcoming public venue was verified.

features.name: Wellrose, Peat Inn
features.fullDescription: Circa 1860 with 20th century additions. Originally 3 cottages. Single-storey, whin rubble with large stugged and droved ashlar dressings, each with central door and 2 window, southern cottage unaltered except for rear wing, middle cottage has later wooden porch. Southern end 20th century, has transverse addition projecting front and back at south end. Original glazing centre and north end. Pantiled roof with 3 droved ashlar stacks, central one harled.

features.name: The Peat Inn, Peat Inn
features.fullDescription: Late 18th/early 19th century. Much altered. Main house 2-storey and attic, rubble with droved ashlar dressings, whitewashed with painted sills and ingoes, 3 window front, central single-storey porch with cornice. Gabled slated roof, straight skews and corniced ashlar end stacks. Two modern flat-roofed dormers. First floor and attic windows in south gable. Single-storey range to left, much altered. Two-storey addition to east with piended roof of modern tiles and slated lean-to outshot to front. Garage and other additions to rear.

features.name: Drumhead, Peat Inn
features.fullDescription: Dated 1745. Two-storey, harl pointed boulder rubble with ashlar dressings at openings. Three window front with central keyblocked door. Door and centre first floor window only have margins. Ground floor windows enlarged early 19th century (original glazing). Pantiled roof with crowstepped gables with skewputts, end stacks rebuilt in brick.

features.name: Cottage, Braeside Terrace, Peat Inn
features.fullDescription: Mid 19th century. Unusually long row of single-storey whin rubble cottages on sloping site, roof slopes with ground. Harled brick dressings at doors and windows and large stugged dressings, some margins painted. Eight double-leaf boarded doors and 14 12-pane sash and case windows, some boarded up. Pantiled roof and 9 stacks, some ashlar, some harled. Internally 2/3 rooms each. No later additions.
